title: LEBER OPTIC ATROPHY AND DYSTONIA
alt_titles: LEBER HEREDITARY OPTIC NEUROPATHY WITH DYSTONIA
DYSTONIA, FAMILIAL, WITH VISUAL FAILURE AND STRIATAL LUCENCIES

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in one of several mitochondrial genes encoding subunits of complex I: MTND6, MTND4, MTND1, and MTND3.

checks.claim: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is caused by mutation in one of several mitochondrial genes encoding subunits of complex I.
checks.evidence_quote: This family has similar clinical characteristics as the previously described families with LHON and dystonia with an ND6 mutation.
checks.explanation: The abstract links LHON/dystonia to ND1 (this family) and ND6 (previous families) only. It does not support the broader claim of several complex I genes, including MTND4 and MTND3.

checks.claim: Mutation in MTND6 can cause Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
checks.explanation: The abstract links an ND6 mutation to LHON and/or dystonia.

checks.claim: Mutation in MTND4 can cause Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.
checks.explanation: The ND4 mutation co-occurs with the ND6 mutation, and the abstract links both together to the phenotype. It does not establish that ND4 alone is causal.

checks.claim: Mutation in MTND1 can cause Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.

checks.claim: Mutation in MTND3 can cause Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

paragraphs.text: Leber optic atrophy and dystonia (LDYT) is a maternally inherited mitochondrial disorder. Affected members of a family show varying combinations of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and progressive generalized dystonia, which is associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions (Novotny et al., 1986; Jun et al., 1994; Wang et al., 2009).

checks.evidence_quote: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions was studied.
checks.explanation: The paper describes maternal transmission and an mtDNA mutation.

checks.claim: In LDYT, affected members of a family show varying combinations of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and progressive generalized dystonia.
checks.evidence_quote: Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT) is a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.
checks.explanation: Variable combinations of vision loss (LHON) and progressive generalized dystonia are stated.

checks.claim: The progressive generalized dystonia in LDYT is associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions.
checks.evidence_quote: 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration
checks.explanation: The paper attributes the dystonia to striatal degeneration, which is basal ganglia involvement. The abstract does not mention lesions or say they are bilateral.

paragraphs.text: Marsden et al. (1986) described 7 members of 2 families with dystonia, which in some patients was accompanied by subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy. All had striking bilateral symmetric lucencies on CT scan, mainly in the putamen. The authors noted that the disorder might be a variant of Leigh disease but that it differed considerably from pathologically proven Leigh disease.

paragraphs.text: Jun et al. (1994) amplified by PCR and sequenced more than 90% of the buffy coat mtDNA from a severely affected child in a Hispanic family with LDYT. The mtDNA belonged to Native American haplogroup D and differed from the Cambridge sequence at 40 positions. One of these differences was a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the MTND6 gene, which caused an ala72-to-val substitution at a moderately conserved residue. The variant was not found in 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs, 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs. Six maternal relatives across 3 generations carried the mutation. One of them, a female with LHON, was heteroplasmic.

paragraphs.text: In a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, De Vries et al. (1996) found none of the mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON. Sequencing of the mitochondrial protein-coding genes identified 2 previously unreported mutations. The first was a heteroplasmic A-to-G transition at nucleotide 11696 in the MTND4 gene, causing a val312-to-ile substitution. The second was a homoplasmic T-to-A change at nucleotide 14596 in the MTND6 gene, causing an ile26-to-met substitution. A muscle biopsy showed severe complex I deficiency, which the authors proposed as the link between these mutations and the phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Spruijt et al. (2007) screened the complete mtDNA of a patient with LHON who lacked the 3 primary LHON mutations. They identified a 3697G-A mutation in the MTND1 gene, which appeared to be associated with isolated complex I deficiency. The authors concluded that this mutation caused both LHON and spastic dystonia in the same family. They noted that the mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome and suggested that other genetic factors may contribute to its clinical expression.

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients, Wang et al. (2009) sequenced the entire mitochondrial genome using a resequencing microarray. They identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene, on a haplogroup D4b background, that substituted threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47. Quantitative analysis showed the mutation to be homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. The authors noted that this mutation had recently been reported in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.

checks.claim: The MTND1 3697G-A mutation appeared to be associated with isolated complex I deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.

checks.claim: Spruijt et al. (2007) noted that the MTND1 3697G-A mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: This mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome

paragraphs.text: In a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients, Wang et al. (2009) identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene, on a haplogroup D4b background, that substituted threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 (A47T). They found it by sequencing the entire mitochondrial genome with a resequencing microarray. The mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. It had previously been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.

checks.claim: In a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients, Wang et al. (2009) identified a 10197G-A mutation in the MTND3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients. The comprehensive nucleotide sequence analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome using resequencing microarray revealed a mutation (mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A))

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation in the Chinese LDYT family was on a haplogroup D4b background.
checks.evidence_quote: at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation substitutes threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 (A47T).
checks.evidence_quote: substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; A47T is the equivalent notation.

checks.claim: Wang et al. (2009) found the MTND3 10197G-A mutation by sequencing the entire mitochondrial genome with a resequencing microarray.
checks.evidence_quote: The comprehensive nucleotide sequence analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome using resequencing microarray revealed a mutation

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side of the Chinese family.
checks.evidence_quote: Quantitative analysis of the heteroplasmy of the mutation revealed a homoplasmy in the leukocytes of all the affected individuals on the maternal side.

checks.claim: The MTND3 10197G-A mutation had previously been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation has recently been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; the draft's 'previously' matches the paper's 'recently'.
